qmd.network: local queries; initial package/model download may require network
qmd.policy: manual install only until a stable release newer than 2.6.3 with project-local trust-gate fixes is verified; Ratchetry never auto-installs or auto-updates QMD

graphify.network: review the selected processing mode before use; do not assume every input remains local
graphify.policy: manual/on-demand architecture tool; prefer for broad architecture queries in large repositories when already installed

serena.network: uvx may download the package; MCP runs locally after installation
serena.benchmark: required against native search before default activation
serena.policy: one primary code-retrieval engine at a time; use only when symbolic navigation beats native search

context7.network: required; repository context and queries leave the local machine
context7.benchmark: not a token optimizer; justify by documentation freshness
context7.policy: enable per project/task only when current third-party documentation is required

ast-grep.benchmark: not required when syntax awareness is necessary
ast-grep.policy: use for syntax-aware patterns that plain text search cannot answer reliably

gitleaks.benchmark: measure false positives and scan latency before mandatory local gating
gitleaks.policy: explicit pre-commit/release scan; never inspect denied credential files outside the repository

rtk.network: local filtering; upstream telemetry is opt-in and should remain disabled for the baseline
rtk.benchmark: required against raw commands with failure-output fallback verified
rtk.policy: optional compression for known verbose commands; preview integration changes and preserve raw failure output

ccusage.network: usage analysis is local; use --offline to prevent pricing refresh access
ccusage.benchmark: measurement source, not itself evidence of savings
ccusage.policy: optional local multi-agent usage observability; snapshots retain aggregates only

trivy.network: vulnerability databases and remote targets may require network
trivy.benchmark: measure database/download cost and scan latency per project profile
trivy.policy: prefer as a consolidated explicit scanner for container/IaC/release profiles; not a per-tool-call hook

semgrep.network: depends on rules and product mode; local rules can run locally
semgrep.benchmark: measure relevant findings, false positives, and latency
semgrep.policy: explicit CI/on-demand SAST for code-bearing projects; never run a heavy scan on every tool call

checkov.network: local scans are possible; integrations and external modules may require network
checkov.policy: recommend only when Terraform, Kubernetes, CloudFormation, or related IaC is detected

osv-scanner.network: advisory database queries/downloads may require network
osv-scanner.benchmark: compare overlap and incremental findings against Trivy
osv-scanner.policy: security-heavy dependency profile only when it adds findings beyond the primary scanner

syft.network: local artifact inventory; registry/image access may require network
syft.benchmark: not required when a release contract requires CycloneDX/SPDX output
syft.policy: supply-chain profile only; Ratchetry already emits an SPDX release SBOM without Syft

grype.network: vulnerability database and registry access may require network
grype.benchmark: compare incremental findings and latency against Trivy
grype.policy: supply-chain/container profile only when it adds evidence beyond the primary scanner

context-mode.network: MCP/tool calls inherit their destinations; package installation requires network
context-mode.benchmark: required against RTK and raw tools because schemas/hooks add their own context and trust surface
context-mode.policy: tool-heavy A/B trials only; never combine with every other output optimizer by default

agent-scan.network: external service/token may be required; review current data flow before use
agent-scan.benchmark: measure detection value, false positives, latency, and external-data exposure
agent-scan.policy: MCP-heavy profile only after explicit data-flow and command-execution review; not a local-first core dependency

ai-jail.network: off by default; enabling --network grants unrestricted network to the sandboxed workload
ai-jail.benchmark: require platform-specific escape/failure tests and workflow overhead evidence against native client sandboxing
ai-jail.policy: manual outer filesystem-isolation experiment only; never replace native Claude/Codex sandboxing, never enable agent state, inherited environment, Docker, host IPC, or network implicitly, and prefer a disposable VM for hostile code

ai-memory.network: loopback-only is possible; team/multi-machine use introduces an authenticated network service and optional model providers
ai-memory.benchmark: require a one-of trial against curated Vault memory for retrieval quality, injected context, storage/privacy, latency, and cost
ai-memory.policy: manual team/multi-machine memory experiment only; do not combine with the default curated Vault path, review hook capture and raw sanitized segments first, and keep LLM/providers disabled for the baseline
